nodes.description: Constant hardcoded address of the legacy TrueUSD token contract (0x8dd5fbCe...); external contract trusted implicitly by the helper.
Constant hardcoded address of the new TrueUSD token contract (0x0000000000085d47...); receives ownership and storage.
Constant hardcoded address of the TokenController contract that is granted ownership over the token contracts.
Constant registry address configured into the TokenController via setTusdRegistry.
Constant global pause address configured into the TokenController via setGlobalPause.
Public upgrade() function with no access control that reassigns ownership of TokenController, oldTrueUSD and newTrueUSD and migrates storage to the new implementation.
Implicit caller of the public upgrade(); never validated, so any external account can trigger the full ownership/state migration.
External call that makes UpgradeHelper the owner of the TokenController, enabling all subsequent privileged operations.
External call that makes UpgradeHelper the owner of the new TrueUSD contract.
External read of oldTrueUSD.totalSupply() and privileged write of the new token supply; unguarded and depends on the answer of the legacy contract.
External call that repoints the legacy token's delegation to the new token; the legacy contract is re-entered and can call back into the helper.
External call transferring TokenController ownership to the owner captured at the start of the unguarded upgrade flow.
Locally cached value of tokenController.owner() used as the final ownership recipient.
Locally cached oldTrueUSD.balances() address reclaimed from the legacy token and moved to the new token.
Locally cached oldTrueUSD.allowances() address reclaimed from the legacy token and moved to the new token.

edges.reason: Any external account (msg.sender) may invoke the public upgrade() function; there is no owner/onlyOwner guard, so an attacker can hijack the entire ownership migration.
upgrade() unconditionally executes tokenController.claimOwnership() as part of the privileged migration sequence.
upgrade() unconditionally executes newTrueUSD.claimOwnership() during the migration.
upgrade() sets the new token supply from the legacy token supply.
upgrade() delegates the legacy token to the new token contract.
upgrade() finally transfers TokenController ownership to the previously cached owner; whoever triggers the flow controls when this privileged transfer happens.
The hardcoded tokenController state variable is the target of the claimOwnership() call.
The hardcoded newTrueUSD state variable is the target of the claimOwnership() call.
The hardcoded newTrueUSD state variable is the target of setTotalSupply().
The supply written to the new token is read from the legacy oldTrueUSD contract.
The legacy oldTrueUSD contract is the receiver of delegateToNewContract().
The new token address is the argument that the legacy token is delegated to.
The hardcoded tokenController is the contract whose ownership is transferred away.
The cached endOwner local determines the final owner of the TokenController.
delegateToNewContract() performs an external call to the legacy token; a hostile or compromised oldTrueUSD can re-enter upgrade() mid-migration and desynchronise the ownership handover.
The external claimOwnership() call to the TokenController can execute arbitrary code in the callee, allowing re-entry into upgrade() before state/ownership is finalised.

normalization_plan.reason: Temporary local that only carries the pre-upgrade TokenController owner into the final transferOwnership call and has no independent security semantics.
Temporary local holding the legacy balance sheet address reclaimed and re-transferred within the same unguarded upgrade() flow.
Temporary local holding the legacy allowance sheet address reclaimed and re-transferred within the same unguarded upgrade() flow.
